entry.title: BIP 110: update status to closed
entry.summary:
The recent attempt to deploy BIP 110 in the Bitcoin network did not meet the required support and consequently failed in both phases of its deployment. It achieved a meager signaling of just under 2.5% of blocks during the latest period, significantly below the threshold needed for acceptance. This low level of support resulted in RDTS nodes, which mandated signaling for this proposal, isolating themselves on a separate chain that managed to mine only two blocks. Meanwhile, the main Bitcoin blockchain continued to grow robustly, adding 134 blocks in the same period. The situation was further compounded when the sole miner on the RDTS chaintip ceased operations, leaving the chain effectively inactive.
Given these developments, it appears that the Bitcoin community has decisively rejected the soft fork proposed by BIP 110. This outcome has led to discussions regarding a possible hard fork among those still interested in the changes proposed by BIP 110. However, as the RDTS chaintip now operates independently with a minority hashrate, it essentially constitutes a new altcoin. According to the guidelines of the BIPs repository, topics concerning altcoins are considered off-topic. Therefore, it is recommended that BIP 110 be transitioned from its current 'Deployed' status to 'Closed,' reflecting its obsolescence and rejection by the network.
